title: Jayden Reed’s Limb Movement Issue Keeps Him From Rejoining Team, NBC Sports Reports
body:
Green Bay’s promising rookie wideout Jayden Reed was forced to exit Sunday’s dramatic 20‑17 overtime victory over the New York Jets after sustaining a neck injury on the second play of the contest. While the team’s medical staff confirmed that Reed exhibits movement in all four extremities, the severity of the trauma prompted coaches to keep him out of travel with the squad, leaving his short‑term availability in question.

Reed, who entered the game as a third‑down specialist, was hit hard by Jets linebacker Demar Dotson just moments after snapping the ball. The collision knocked the 22‑year‑old down and left him visibly shaken, prompting an immediate assessment on the field. Though he was able to sit up and move his arms and legs, the concussion protocol and precautionary measures for neck injuries dictated that he be removed from further play. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur later addressed the situation, emphasizing that Reed’s “neurological function remains intact” but that the team would err on the side of caution before allowing him to rejoin the roster for upcoming travel.

The incident arrives at a pivotal juncture for the Packers, who have been navigating a season marked by offensive inconsistency and a thin receiving corps. Reed’s emergence has been a bright spot; he has logged 27 receptions for 298 yards and two touchdowns since being elevated from the practice squad earlier this month. His speed and route‑running acumen have given quarterback Jordan Love an additional weapon, especially in red‑zone scenarios where Reed’s size—6’2”, 210 pounds—creates mismatches against smaller defensive backs. Losing him, even temporarily, forces Green Bay to rely more heavily on veteran veterans such as Marquez Valdes‑Scantling and rookie sensation Romeo Doubs, both of whom have struggled to find consistent rhythm this season.

Medical experts caution that neck injuries, even those that appear minor, can have lingering effects that extend beyond the immediate game. Dr. Emily Hargrove, a sports medicine physician who has consulted with NFL teams, explained that “any impact to the cervical spine warrants a thorough evaluation, including imaging and neurological testing, before clearing an athlete for full contact.” The Packers’ decision to keep Reed off the team bus aligns with league‑wide trends toward heightened player safety, especially after the NFL’s recent amendments to concussion and spinal injury protocols. The league now mandates that any player exhibiting signs of neck trauma undergo a minimum of 48 hours of observation, followed by a graduated return‑to‑play protocol that can span several weeks.

From a strategic perspective, Reed’s absence could influence the Packers’ approach in their upcoming matchup against the Detroit Lions, a game that will likely hinge on the ability of the offense to stretch the field. If Reed remains sidelined, Green Bay may need to adjust its play‑calling, incorporating more short‑passing concepts and increased reliance on the running game to mitigate the risk of further injuries. Conversely, a swift and clean recovery could see Reed return as a spark plug, providing LaFleur with the flexibility to design more aggressive downfield routes that could exploit Detroit’s secondary, which has struggled against speed receivers this season.

Looking ahead, the Packers’ medical staff is expected to release a detailed update within the next 24‑48 hours, outlining Reed’s diagnostic results and projected timeline. While the team hopes for a rapid return, the priority remains the athlete’s long‑term health and the integrity of the roster. Should Reed be cleared, his comeback will be closely watched not only by Green Bay fans eager for another offensive catalyst but also by league officials monitoring the effectiveness of the new safety protocols. In the meantime, the Packers must adapt, balancing the urgency of a playoff push with the responsibility of safeguarding a young talent whose future contributions could be pivotal to the franchise’s success.
